summary.title: Quick guide to web typography for developers
summary.one_liner: You learn the handful of CSS typography settings (font choice and format, font size, line height, line width, letter-spacing, text wrapping, font smoothing) that make web text readable with minimal effort.
takeaways: Use system-ui or a well-chosen local font for fast loading, or self-host WOFF2 fonts via @font-face when you need custom typefaces.
Set root font size in percentages and other sizes in rem so user browser font settings are respected.
Use unitless line-height around 1.5 for body text and roughly 1.15 to 1.3 for headings; limit line width to about 45 to 100 characters by constraining the container.
Use variable fonts for multiple weights, text-wrap: balance to avoid orphans in titles, and text-size-adjust and font smoothing for mobile and macOS tweaks.
summary.summary: The author, a web developer, gives an 80/20 guide to typography for developers without designers. It covers font selection (system fonts, external WOFF2 files, variable fonts, subsetting), size and spacing (percent on root, rem elsewhere, typographic scale, line height, line width, letter-spacing), colour and contrast, hierarchy, and text wrapping. It ends with browser quirks such as mobile text-size-adjust and macOS font smoothing, plus further reading including Butterick's Practical Typography.
